doc: Ch7 'The Tidecup' (M3-C07-02; docs/kb/story/beats/act1_ch07.md B01-B10; docs/kb/tech/chapter_flow.md 'Ch7'). Two greybox zones, played by ZoneStory: ch07/tamsule (the port) and ch07/tamsule_bell_galleries (the story's stand-in for the Bell's galleries, pool and moorings; the arena itself, ch07/tamsule_bell, is env-art's and the Reefball agent's). ENTRY: Ch6 (not built) will hand off to ch07/tamsule at RiverMouth; until then the zone is reached from its own locations.json row. The port: B01 on arrival (the chapter becomes 7, the chapter autosave), the B02 barks, B03 when Rhen walks on to the market boats (Tavi; Pio's side-band), then the gantry foot to the Bell. The Bell: B04 on arrival (the galleries; then Rhen on the pool steps and a checkpoint autosave, so a reload starts at the rim), B05 at the rim (the naming), which ends on <<event start_reefball tidecup_opening>>. THE REEFBALL SEAM is the beat 'reefball_match' in ch07/tamsule_bell_galleries, run by the naming beat's if_event step. Today it is a STAND-IN: it sets ch07_tidecup_played (never ch07_tidecup_won: the stand-in reports no win) and travels back to this zone at CatchPool, the same return the real match makes. The Reefball agent replaces that beat's steps (and only them) with the hand-off to the match scene; the match must set ch07_tidecup_played always, ch07_tidecup_won on a win only (a reward, never read by the story), give its own rewards, and return to ch07/tamsule_bell_galleries at CatchPool, where the arrival row plays B07 identically for both results. B07 sets ch07_tavi_withdrew; then the moorings side scene (B09, Tavi at his boat; it takes Pio's band, and the Pemakar leaf-boat if Rhen kept it) and the way back to the port. The port's barks swap to their after-match variants (B08). B10 at the harbour. EXIT: Ch8's ch08/corrow is not built, so B10 hands off to the end card; Ch8 replaces that step with {"go": {"location": "ch08/corrow", ...}}. Ch7 has no foes. Party: Rhen, Asha and Toma, with Ysolde in reserve (Liss and Kerrid have no battle rows yet; they are stage actors).
